newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Bounce in U.S. stocks may be short lived.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bounce in U.S. stocks may be short lived.

text.p: U.S. stocks appeared to be stabilizing on Friday after a sharp week-long selloff but it will be days or weeks before the damage is repaired enough to support a lasting rebound, technical analysts said.
Until solid technical support is established, any bounce in stocks could be short lived, they said.
"You want to be on the sidelines, generally speaking, and not play rallies because rallies are going to hit some resistance on the way up," said Jonathan Dodd, technical analyst at Dean Witter.
Chart watchers pointed to a bounce in the battered Nasdaq composite as a sign the broader market could be probing its near-term lows.

The Nasdaq composite closed at 1201 on Wednesday, after a brief intra-day dip below the 1200 mark. The index jumped nearly 13 points on Thursday and was up another 11 points, or about one percent, at 1225 in early afternoon trading Friday.
Before the bounce, the Nasdaq index had fallen 13.5 percent off its January 22 high as investors concerned over rising interest rates punished high-growth technology stocks.

"I think that's about it for now," Gary Kaltbaum technical analyst J.W. Charles. "I'm not sayng we're not in a bear market because you do get bounces in bear markets. But I think right now it's the bottom, definitely for the Nasdaq and more likely for the market in general."
While the Nasdaq found near-term support at the 1200 level, technical analysts said 6400 was a key Dow level.
The Dow was down about 57 points at 6429 after tumbling to a session low of 6405.
With Friday's drop, the Dow has fallen about nine percent off its March 11 high.
Dodd said that any low point on the major stock indices had to hold for a sufficient period of time, perhaps several weeks, before it could be read as potential support.
"You have to have a low made, and then test that," he said. "You don't have that" yet, he said.
He said initial resistance appeared in the 6750-6800 range on the Dow and around 1250 on the Nasdaq composite.

Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities, also said he expected to see a "stabilization period" running for several sessions before stocks would be in a position for mount a rebound with positive technical characteristics.
But he said he expected the rebound to come, noting that the selloff had not been accompanied by expanding trading volume normally seen with major stock market reversals.
"I believe we will recover from this, primarily because volume has been moderate for seven weeks now," he said.
